To: Emma Cole <emma.cole@acmehealth.com>, contracts@acmehealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form liability carve-outs & OSS/model license liability

Hi Emma —

Great to be moving toward an Order Form. Legal at Acme flagged a couple of items in the MSA/Order Form redlines around liability caps and carve-outs for open-source/model licensing. High level: they want clearer language around (a) whether OSS-related claims are excluded from the liability cap or carved out as pass-through liability, and (b) whether consequential damages are excluded in ways that would preclude recoveries for third-party IP/license claims.

Can you confirm whether the Acme team is seeking a full indemnity pass-through for OSS (i.e., unlimited or uncapped obligations for claims caused by OSS licensing defects) or a limited pass-through tied to direct damages with a dollar cap? If you can share the redlines, I’ll loop in our contracts/legal folks and propose alternative wording that preserves our commercial protections while addressing Acme’s compliance concerns.

Proposed next step: redlines from Acme → our legal gives one-pass counter language → short call if needed.

Attaching: Redwood standard Order Form + MSA reference for quick review (no attachments in this initial email).

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thanks. Attaching Acme's redlines (Acme_Redlines_2026-03-29.pdf). Key asks from our counsel:

- Carve OSS and model licensing claims out of the limitation of liability (we're proposing pass-through for third-party claims arising from OSS or licensed model components).
- If Redwood insists on any cap for OSS pass-through, we'd like a separate, higher cap (we proposed $250k).
- Preserve customer remedies for downstream damages caused by license violations (we need consequential damages to be available when they arise from third-party IP or licensing claims).
- Contractual assurance that Redwood will promptly notify and cooperate with Acme on any third-party OSS claim.

We're open to Redwood proposing specific language to balance commercial risk. Happy to join a call next week with our legal if that helps.

Emma Cole
Head of Vendor Contracts | Acme Health
emma.cole@acmehealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 15:20:45 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form liability carve-outs & OSS/model license liability

Alex / team / Emma —

Thanks for the redlines, Emma. I reviewed Acme's proposals and sketched a middle-ground that we can use in our counter. Main points:

1) Limitation of liability: keep an aggregate cap tied to fees (e.g., 12 months of fees) for contractual breaches and service failures, but carve out a narrow set of claims from the cap: (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality, and (iii) third-party IP infringement claims where Redwood has been found liable.

2) OSS/model licensing: we cannot accept an uncapped pass-through indemnity for OSS. Open-source components are often used under permissive licenses and upstream dependencies — we need to limit exposure. Proposed approach: Redwood will (a) indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging Redwood-delivered model or software infringes on third-party IP to the extent caused by Redwood modifications or distribution, and (b) for OSS-licensed components, Redwood will provide defense and indemnity only for direct damages resulting from a breach of a specific OSS license that Redwood bundled, subject to a separate OSS-specific sub-cap of $250,000 aggregate.

3) Consequential damages: we can agree to exclude consequential/incidental damages generally, but carve back recovery where such damages arise directly from a third-party IP or license claim (i.e., if a court awards Acme downstream losses because of an IP injunction tied to a Redwood-delivered model, Acme can recover those). This keeps the general commercial barrier intact but protects customers from unusual IP license fallout.

4) Notice & cooperation: we accept prompt notice/cooperation obligations; Redwood should retain control of defense with reasonable input from Acme and the ability to select counsel. Acme can reserve the right to intervene if Redwood fails to defend diligently.

I attached a doc with markup (Redwood_Proposed_Liability_Wording_2026-03-30.docx) that tracks specific clause language. If the Acme team is comfortable with a $250k OSS sub-cap, I think we can get to a signed Order Form quickly. If they insist on an uncapped pass-through, that's a material commercial escalation and will need approval from Finance/Legal leadership.

Suggested next step: short legal-to-legal call to confirm OSS cap and whether Acme needs per-claim vs. aggregate treatment. I'm available Mon/Tue mornings next week.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Liability_Wording_2026-03-30.docx (Word, 12 KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Cole <emma.cole@acmehealth.com>, contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form liability carve-outs & OSS/model license liability

Quick note to clarify the cap framing Neha proposed:

- Redwood suggests the $250k OSS sub-cap be aggregate (all OSS-related claims in the term), not per-claim. That prevents catastrophic multiple small claims from exceeding expectations across the contract term.
- For the main LOB cap we proposed 12 months of fees (we should confirm the exact MRR/committed amount with Sales before lock).
- If Acme feels strongly about per-claim treatment, that would be a commercial concession; we should only do that with approval from Revenue Ops/Finance.

Also, we should confirm whether Acme wants the carve-out to apply to both open-source components used in our runtime and any licensed third-party models we serve. My read: for third-party licensed models where Redwood is only a distributor (we serve unmodified vendor models), pass-through risk is higher; we may need to exclude those from indemnity entirely and require the vendor to indemnify. That's a downstream dependency to call out.

-Priyom
Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Emma Cole <emma.cole@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 16:45:51 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form liability carve-outs & OSS/model license liability

Neha / Priyom / Alex —

Thanks for the clear options and wording. Acme is willing to accept the $250k OSS aggregate sub-cap (we appreciate the clarity) and the 12 months-of-fees aggregate cap for other liabilities. Our counsel wants the OSS carve-out to cover open-source components that Redwood bundles or distributes as part of the service; for third-party vendor models (where Redwood acts as a reseller/distributor of an upstream model), Acme requests that Redwood confirm in the Order Form which models are vendor-managed vs. Redwood-managed and that vendor-managed models will remain subject to the upstream vendor's license and indemnity terms (i.e., Acme reserves the right to pursue the vendor).

We'd like the final redline set to reflect: (1) aggregate caps as discussed, (2) OSS sub-cap $250k, (3) carveback for consequential damages specifically resulting from third-party IP/license claims, (4) Redwood retains defense control with Acme intervention rights on material IP suits, and (5) a representation that Redwood will provide a list of third-party/vendor models with their licensing stance prior to execution.

Can Redwood send a tracked-redline Order Form with the OSS sub-cap language and a short appendix listing the vendor-managed models we typically offer? If so, we can turn this into a DocuSign-ready package after a final 30-minute legal call.

Best —
Emma Cole
Head of Vendor Contracts | Acme Health
Attachment: Acme_Final_Points_2026-03-30.msg (MSG, 18 KB)
